subject: Re: Demo follow-up — evaluation sprint & parity acceptance path
messages:
From: Sana Shah <sana@ledgerly.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + demo follow-up: Ledgerly model evaluation

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier — great context from both of you. A quick recap from my side and asks so we can scope a short evaluation sprint: 

- Goal: replace a portion of our in-house NLU routing with an inference stack that matches our production baseline on intent-match and reduces hallucination on payment reconciliation prompts.
- Key constraints: PII in prompts (tokenized), 24h retention requirement for logs, and p50 latency target of ~300ms for short prompts.

Could you send:
1) recommended model candidates (open variants you suggest we trial) and the proprietary baseline comparison approach;
2) a sample prompt set we can use for parity checks;
3) a proposed timeline and acceptance thresholds for a 1–2 week sprint.

Also looping in Oliver (ops) on procurement timing. If we can get a proposed plan by end of day Monday that would be awesome. 

Thanks,
Sana Shah
Head of Product, Ledgerly
https://ledgerly.com

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Sana Shah <sana@ledgerly.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo follow-up: Ledgerly model evaluation

Thanks Sana — appreciate the clear constraints. Draft plan below; attaching a one-sheet sprint plan and the initial prompt bundle for your review.

Attachments: 20270815-ledgerly-eval-sprint-plan.xlsx (proposal), prompt-bundle-v1.jsonl (sample prompts)

TL;DR proposed eval sprint (2 weeks, can compress to 1 week with dataset prep from Ledgerly):
- Candidates: Llama2-70B-q4f16 (open), RedMod-13B-8bit (Redwood-verified), Redwood-prop baseline variant (internal tuned baseline used only for comparison).
- Acceptance thresholds (initial):
  - Intent match (business-critical prompts): >= 94% relative to proprietary baseline OR within 5 percentage points absolute (whichever is tighter).
  - Hallucination rate on critical reconciliation prompts: <= 2.5% (we'll define sample set).
  - Safety regression: no new high-severity safety findings on our safety probe suite.
  - Performance: p50 latency < 300ms on your short prompt distribution (we'll run p50/p95 on a 500-sample replay).
- Cost target: aim for <= 0.40x of your current per-call inference cost for matched quality on candidate open models (estimable after first pass).

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Ledgerly shares 500 de-identified replay prompts + 50 labeled critical reconciliation prompts (we provided a template in the attached prompt-bundle).
2) Redwood runs open-model pass + our tuned baseline comparison; share detailed CSV with metrics and failure examples.
3) Joint readout + decision: pass / canary / reject with mitigation plan.

Related links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ledgerly/HL-24319
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/ledgerly/2027/eval-sprint/overview

If that sounds right I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Wednesday to align on data format and NDA/procurement touchpoints.

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sana Shah <sana@ledgerly.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, Oliver Grant <oliver@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2027-08-16T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo follow-up: Ledgerly model evaluation

Thanks — the proposal is helpful. A few clarifications and concerns from our side before we hand over the replay set: 

- Parity definition: For procurement we need "parity" to be concrete. Ledgerly's legal wants intent-match within 5% absolute of our current baseline on the labeled critical set, and hallucination strictly lower than the baseline. If an open model meets tighter intent-match but has slightly higher hallucination, that will be a blocker.
- Data handling / compliance: we operate in a regulated payments vertical. Can you confirm the Redwood Private option (VPC) or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS is available if we need it for the production rollout? We need SOC2 and KMS details for procurement.
- Please include Monica (procurement) on security/compliance evidence and any high-level cost estimate for Dedicated capacity.

We'll scope the de-identification and share the 500 replays by EOD Tuesday assuming the kickoff is scheduled.

Sana
Head of Product, Ledgerly

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sana Shah <sana@ledgerly.com>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-16T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo follow-up: Ledgerly model evaluation

Looping in a slightly more prescriptive acceptance path and gating plan so procurement and product are aligned. Attachment: ledgerly_parity_benchmarks.csv (example output format).

Key points:
- Concrete acceptance gate (final):
  1) Intent-match (macro): open-model candidate >= (baseline_intent - 5pp) AND not worse on the labeled critical set by > 2pp.
  2) Hallucination: candidate <= baseline_hallucination (we'll measure using your critical prompt probe).
  3) Latency/cost: p50 under target and estimated per-call cost within the cost target provided by Priyom.
- If a candidate passes metrics but shows concentrated failures on a semantic class (e.g., refund-edge-cases), we'll propose targeted prompt engineering + small supervised fine-tune before canarying.
- Rollout plan on pass: 1% canary (non-critical traffic) for 48h, automatic rollback on +10% degraded intent-match or >1.5x hallucination spike vs baseline.

Security/compliance note (Monica): Redwood Private (VPC) is available; we can provide SOC 2 type II report, KMS/HSM integration docs and redact checklist as part of the procurement artifact bundle. We'll mirror the required evidence to your security team before the readout.

Example deliverables we will share after the sweep: CSV with per-prompt metrics, 20 worst-case failure traces (with de-identified tokens), latency distribution, cost projection.

Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Sana Shah <sana@ledgerly.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Great — thanks all. Quick logistics to lock the kickoff and next actions: 

1) Kickoff: Wednesday 2027-08-18 10:00am PT (30m) — I’ll send calendar invite once I get a quick confirmation from Ledgerly.
2) Data: Sana to upload the 500 de-identified replays + 50 labeled critical prompts to the shared Drive link by EOD Tuesday. Use the template in prompt-bundle-v1.jsonl; we’ll confirm format on the kickoff.
3) Procurement/security: Monica will share SOC2 & KMS docs in the procurement thread and open a ticket for Dedicated pricing if Ledgerly prefers reserved capacity.
4) Deliverables & timing: Redwood run (48–72h after data receipt) → preliminary CSV + failure examples → joint readout within 3 business days of run.

Action items (assignments):
- Sana: confirm kickoff and upload dataset (Ledgerly)
- Monica: share evidence bundle and pricing options (Redwood)
- Marissa/Vivek: own metrics pass/fail criteria and runscript; Priyom will coordinate the execution.

If that timeline works I’ll send the invite and update the sprint plan spreadsheet.

Thanks,
